input: Draft terms and conditions for my freelance services

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Freelance T&Cs vary enormously by service type — a developer's IP clauses differ from a photographer's usage rights or a copywriter's revision policy. Knowing the exact service(s) shapes which clauses are essential.
Who the clients are (individuals, small businesses, enterprises, international) affects the legal language, jurisdiction, and formality level needed.
Whether the user needs a legally vetted document or a practical working template changes how rigorous and lawyer-ready the draft needs to be.
The country or region determines which governing law applies, what consumer-protection rules must be observed, and which legal terms are enforceable.
The intended format (standalone PDF, embedded on a website, appended to a proposal) affects structure, length, and how the document is presented.
Tone (plain English vs. formal legal language) affects readability and how clients receive the document — a casual creative agency and a corporate contractor need very different registers.
Knowing which clauses the user most wants to protect — payment terms, IP ownership, revision limits, liability cap — lets the plan prioritise the sections that matter most.

gold.taskTitle: Draft Terms and Conditions for Freelance Services
gold.taskDescription: Write a terms and conditions document that governs the user's freelance service agreements with clients.

questions.title: What type of freelance service do you provide?
questions.description: Identifies the specific service (e.g., web development, graphic design, copywriting, consulting) so that service-specific clauses such as IP transfer, usage rights, or deliverable definitions can be included.

questions.title: Who are your typical clients — individuals, businesses, or both?
questions.description: Determines the audience for the T&Cs, which affects formality, liability language, and whether consumer-protection provisions are needed.

questions.title: Which country or region will these T&Cs be governed by?
questions.description: Establishes the applicable governing law and jurisdiction, ensuring the document is legally relevant and enforceable where the user operates.

questions.title: Do you need a lawyer-ready draft or a practical working template?
questions.description: Clarifies the required level of legal rigour — a court-ready document needs precise legal language, while a working template can prioritise clarity and usability.

questions.title: Where will clients read or sign these T&Cs?
questions.description: Determines the format and structure needed — e.g., a PDF attachment to proposals, a page on a website, or a section within a contract document.

questions.title: Should the tone be plain English or formal legal language?
questions.description: Guides the writing style so the document matches the user's brand and feels appropriate to their client relationships.

questions.title: Which clauses matter most — payment, IP ownership, revisions, or liability?
questions.description: Identifies the user's top priorities so the most critical protections are drafted with the greatest care and detail.
